title: Power Rankings: Spurs still surging at No. 1
heading: 2010-11 Power Rankings: Week 15
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Normally I'd agree that the 50-game mark is too soon to be talking about magic numbers when it comes to clinching No. 1 in the West. These Spurs, though, have a seven-game cushion on their closest pursuers.

rankings.summaryHtml: Just as the recent 10-game win streak was actually more impressive than its 11-1 start, New Orleans' post-streak struggles are more worrisome this time. Way more thanks to the injuries to Okafor (oblique) and Ariza (ankle).

rankings.summaryHtml: The Magic were a wobbly 16-9 when they swung their big trades ... and they've slumped to 16-11 since. They're so out of sorts that Dwight, for the first time since December 2006, hasn't blocked a shot for three games.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Grizz wound up going 8-2 in that stretch of 10 games with only one foe possessing a record above .500. Not bad given what's going on with Mayo and compared to last season's second-half fade after a 25-19 start.

rankings.summaryHtml: Some week for the Hawks. They got twice as many All-Stars as I expected (Horford and Joe Johnson) and passed Orlando to move into the East's No. 4 slot right after I suggested they were doomed to No. 5 (at best).

rankings.summaryHtml: The NBA's single-game scoring record on the day of the Super Bowl is Pistol Pete's 50-point game in 1972. In his 50th game as a Knick, Amare made a nice run for it in Sunday's win over Philly with a forceful burst of 41.
